classification.difficultyReason: Identify adjacent and hypotenuse in the supplied triangle, use inverse cosine and apply the explicitly supplied bearing complement before rounding to minutes.

content.prompt:
A rider travelled 4 km due east from $A$ before changing direction and riding due north to $B$.
$B$ is 6 km from $A$. Calculate the true bearing from $A$ to $B$ $(90^\circ-\theta)$. Answer to the nearest minute.

spec.description: Right triangle with compass at A, an eastward horizontal leg, B due north of its endpoint, and the acute angle theta between east and AB. Decorative source colours become black.
spec.mathematics: AC = 4 km, AB = 6 km, CB perpendicular to AC. Coordinates preserve AC/AB = 2/3; the unlabelled northward leg is derived from the givens.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and theta are shown; the bearing and calculated angle are withheld.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\cos\theta &= \frac{4}{6}\\\theta &= \cos^{-1}\!\left(\frac{4}{6}\right)\end{align*}$$
The true bearing is measured clockwise from north:
$$\begin{align*}\text{Bearing} &= 90^\circ-\cos^{-1}\!\left(\frac{4}{6}\right)\\&\approx 041^\circ49'\end{align*}$$
